newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WEBSTER OUTSHINES THE RECORD BREAKERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WEBSTER OUTSHINES THE RECORD BREAKERS.

text.p: England's Steve Webster finished eagle-birdie to capture a two-stroke lead midway through the second round of the English Open on Friday and put two course record-breakers in the shadow.

Webster's six-under-par 66 to move to 10-under-par 134, put him two shots ahead of Northern Ireland's Darren Clarke and three in front of Argentine Jose Coceres, who both finished two better than the previous course record with eight-birdie 64s.
Webster, fourth in the Italian Open two weeks ago, lost his European Tour card last year after having won the 1995 qualifying school.
"I'm not sure what the target for keeping the card will be this year but I don't intend to lose it again," said the 22-year-old Webster.
"I was always struggling last year but I've already proved to myself that my game is in good shape this year by not getting into trouble when I did miss a fairway."
Clarke, lying seventh on the Ryder Cup standings, would seal his Valderrama place with a win this week following victory last year in the German Masters.
"I started playing well again two weeks ago by forgetting about too much technical stuff," said the 28-year-old Ulsterman.
"It was on the advice of my coach, and just going out there playing with my old grip and my old swing gives me encouragement to think I can win again, perhaps win on a regular basis. "
Coceres stormed home with a five under par 31 on the back nine.

"I know I can win because I keep getting close this year," said the 33-year-old Argentine. "One of these times I must go all the way. If my iron play stays as good as today then I have a chance this week."
